requirements.subject: ent:rotate-operator
requirements.canonical: The predefined rotate operators ARE the rotate left operator `<@` and the rotate right operator `@>`.
requirements.original: The predefined rotate operators perform the rotate left (<@) and rotate right (@>) operators.

requirements.subject: ent:left-hand-operand
requirements.canonical: The left-hand operand of a rotate operator SHALL be of root type `bitstring`, `hexstring`, `octetstring`, `charstring`, `universal charstring`, `record of` or `set of`.
requirements.original: Their left-hand operand shall be of root type bitstring, hexstring, octetstring, charstring, universal `charstring,` record of, or set of.

requirements.subject: ent:right-hand-operand
requirements.canonical: The right-hand operand of a rotate operator SHALL be a non-negative integer value.
requirements.original: Their right-hand operand shall be a non-negative integer.

requirements.subject: ent:rotate-operator
requirements.canonical: The result type of a rotate operator SHALL be the root type of its left-hand operand.
requirements.original: The result type of these operators shall be the same as the root type of the left-hand operand.

requirements.subject: ent:array
requirements.canonical: An array MAY be used as the left-hand operand of a rotate operator, because the root type of an array is `record of`.
requirements.original: NOTE 1: Note that the root types of arrays is record of, therefore arrays are allowed as left-hand operands of rotate operators.

requirements.subject: ent:rotate-operator
requirements.canonical: The behaviour of a rotate operator IS determined by the type of its left-hand operand.
requirements.original: The rotate operators behave differently based upon the type of their left-hand operand.

requirements.subject: ent:rotate-unit
requirements.condition: the left-hand operand is of type `bitstring`
requirements.canonical: If the left-hand operand of a rotate operator is of type `bitstring`, the rotate unit applied IS 1 bit.
requirements.original: a) `bitstring then the rotate unit applied is 1 bit;` b) `hexstring then the rotate unit applied is 1 hexadecimal digit;` c) `octetstring then the rotate unit applied is 1 octet;` d) `charstring or universal` `charstring then the rotate unit applied is one character;` e) `record of, set of, or array then the rotate unit applied is one element.` If the type of the left-hand operand is:

requirements.condition: the left-hand operand is of type `hexstring`

requirements.original: a) `bitstring then the rotate unit applied is 1 bit;` b) `hexstring then the rotate unit applied is 1 hexadecimal digit;` c) `octetstring then the rotate unit applied is 1 octet;` d) `charstring or universal` `charstring then the rotate unit applied is one character;` e) `record of, set of, or array then the rotate unit applied is one element.` If the type of the left-hand operand is:

requirements.subject: ent:rotate-unit
requirements.condition: the left-hand operand is of type `octetstring`
requirements.canonical: If the left-hand operand of a rotate operator is of type `octetstring`, the rotate unit applied IS 1 octet.
requirements.original: a) `bitstring then the rotate unit applied is 1 bit;` b) `hexstring then the rotate unit applied is 1 hexadecimal digit;` c) `octetstring then the rotate unit applied is 1 octet;` d) `charstring or universal` `charstring then the rotate unit applied is one character;` e) `record of, set of, or array then the rotate unit applied is one element.` If the type of the left-hand operand is:

requirements.condition: the left-hand operand is of type `charstring` or `universal charstring`
requirements.canonical: If the left-hand operand of a rotate operator is of type `charstring` or `universal charstring`, the rotate unit applied IS one character.
requirements.original: a) `bitstring then the rotate unit applied is 1 bit;` b) `hexstring then the rotate unit applied is 1 hexadecimal digit;` c) `octetstring then the rotate unit applied is 1 octet;` d) `charstring or universal` `charstring then the rotate unit applied is one character;` e) `record of, set of, or array then the rotate unit applied is one element.` If the type of the left-hand operand is:

requirements.subject: ent:rotate-unit
requirements.condition: the left-hand operand is of type `record of`, `set of` or array
requirements.canonical: If the left-hand operand of a rotate operator is of type `record of`, `set of` or array, the rotate unit applied IS one element.
requirements.original: a) `bitstring then the rotate unit applied is 1 bit;` b) `hexstring then the rotate unit applied is 1 hexadecimal digit;` c) `octetstring then the rotate unit applied is 1 octet;` d) `charstring or universal` `charstring then the rotate unit applied is one character;` e) `record of, set of, or array then the rotate unit applied is one element.` If the type of the left-hand operand is:

requirements.subject: ent:rotate-left-operator
requirements.canonical: The rotate left operator `<@` IS a binary operator taking a left-hand and a right-hand operand.
requirements.original: The rotate left (<@) operator accepts two operands.

requirements.subject: ent:rotate-left-operator
requirements.canonical: The rotate left operator `<@` rotates the left-hand operand to the left by the number of rotate units specified by the right-hand operand.
requirements.original: It rotates the left-hand operand by the number of shift units to the left as specified by the right-hand operand.

ambiguity.issue: 'shift units' is used in the rotate clause, while the list above defines 'rotate unit'.

requirements.subject: ent:rotate-left-operator
requirements.canonical: For the rotate left operator `<@`, the rotate units shifted out on the left IS re-inserted into the left-hand operand from its right-hand side.
requirements.original: Excess shift units (bits, hexadecimal digits, octets, characters, or elements) are re-inserted into the left-hand operand from its right-hand side.

ambiguity.issue: 'Excess shift units' is used where 'rotate units' (as defined in the list) is meant.

requirements.subject: ent:left-hand-operand
requirements.condition: the left-hand operand is of a record of, set of or array type
requirements.canonical: When a rotate operator is applied to a `record of`, `set of` or array value, the left-hand operand SHALL be at least partially initialized.
requirements.original: a) When the rotate operator is used for record of-s, set of-s and arrays, its left hand operand shall be at least partially initialized.

requirements.subject: ent:right-hand-operand
requirements.canonical: The right-hand operand of a rotate operator SHALL additionally satisfy restriction a) of clause 6.5.
requirements.original: NOTE 2: Note that for the right hand operand restriction a) in clause 6.5 further on applies.

ambiguity.issue: Clause 6.5 of this version is 'Automatic type', whose item a) does not constrain operands of operators; the reference appears stale, so the intended restriction cannot be determined.
readings: The right-hand operand of a rotate operator SHALL satisfy item a) of clause 6.5 (Automatic type).
The right-hand operand of a rotate operator SHALL satisfy the general operator restriction a) of clause 7.1 (operands shall be initialized/of compatible type), the reference to 6.5 being outdated.

requirements.subject: ent:rotate-right-operator
requirements.canonical: The rotate right operator `@>` IS a binary operator taking a left-hand and a right-hand operand.
requirements.original: The rotate right (@>) operator accepts two operands.

requirements.subject: ent:rotate-right-operator
requirements.canonical: The rotate right operator `@>` rotates the left-hand operand to the right by the number of rotate units specified by the right-hand operand.
requirements.original: It rotates the left-hand operand by the number of shift units to the right as specified by the right-hand operand.

ambiguity.issue: The rule for `@>` is placed inside the Examples block (after EXAMPLE 1) and uses 'shift units' instead of 'rotate units'.

requirements.subject: ent:rotate-right-operator
requirements.canonical: For the rotate right operator `@>`, the rotate units shifted out on the right IS re-inserted into the left-hand operand from its left-hand side.
requirements.original: Excess shift units (bits, hexadecimal digits, octets, characters, or elements) are re-inserted into the left-hand operand from its left-hand side.

ambiguity.issue: The rule is placed inside the Examples block and uses 'shift units' instead of 'rotate units'.

requirements.subject: ent:presence-checking-operator
requirements.canonical: The presence checking operators ARE `ispresent`, `ischosen`, `isvalue` and `isbound`.
requirements.original: The presence checking operators include ispresent, ischosen, isvalue and isbound operators.

requirements.subject: ent:presence-checking-operator
requirements.canonical: The result type of a presence checking operator IS `boolean`.
requirements.original: The result type of the presence checking operators is boolean.

requirements.subject: ent:presence-checking-operator
requirements.canonical: The operand of a presence checking operator MAY be of any type.
requirements.original: The operand of these operators can be of any type.

ambiguity.issue: The general statement conflicts with 7.1.8.2, which allows `ischosen` only for union-field references and anytype alternatives. Chosen reading: any type is allowed in general, the operator-specific clauses may restrict it further.
readings: The operand of every presence checking operator MAY be of any type.
The operand of a presence checking operator MAY be of any type, unless the clause of the specific operator (e.g. 7.1.8.2 for `ischosen`) restricts the operand.

requirements.subject: ent:presence-checking-operator
requirements.canonical: Special error-handling rules apply when the operand of a presence checking operator is a data object reference, function instance, template instance or the result of a `valueof` operation followed by an ExtendedFieldReference.
requirements.original: Specific rules apply if the operand of a presence checking operator is a data object reference, function instance, template instance or a result of the valueof operation followed by an ExtendedFieldReference.

ambiguity.issue: It is unclear whether 'followed by an ExtendedFieldReference' qualifies only the valueof result or all listed operand forms. Chosen reading: all operand forms followed by an ExtendedFieldReference, since the following rules concern resolving the ExtendedFieldReference.
readings: The special rules apply to a data object reference, function instance, template instance or valueof result, each followed by an ExtendedFieldReference.
The special rules apply to any data object reference, function instance or template instance, and to a valueof result only when followed by an ExtendedFieldReference.

requirements.subject: ent:presence-checking-operator
requirements.condition: resolving dot notation, index notation or a decoded field reference in the ExtendedFieldReference of the operand of a presence checking operator would produce an error
requirements.canonical: If resolving the dot notation, index notation or decoded field references of the ExtendedFieldReference of a presence checking operator operand would produce an error (e.g. index out of range, sub-field of an omitted field), the normal error IS NOT raised and the following special handling applies instead.

requirements.canonical: If resolving the ExtendedFieldReference of a presence checking operator operand would produce an error, no error IS produced.
requirements.original: No error is produced. requirements.condition: resolving dot notation, index notation or a decoded field reference in the ExtendedFieldReference of the operand of a presence checking operator would produce an error
requirements.canonical: If resolving the ExtendedFieldReference of a presence checking operator operand would produce an error, evaluation of all remaining unresolved fields of the ExtendedFieldReference IS stopped.
requirements.original: Evaluation of all remaining unresolved fields in the ExtendedFieldReference is stopped. In these cases, if resolving dot notation, index notation (see clause 7.2) or decoded field references (see clause 7.3) included in the _ExtendedFieldReference would produce an error (e.g. if an index is out of range, when referencing a sub-field of an_ omitted field etc.), the following happens:

requirements.subject: ent:presence-checking-operator
requirements.canonical: The special error handling of dot notation, index notation and decoded field references in presence checking operators IS NOT applied recursively.
requirements.original: The rule on special handling of dot notation, index notation and decoded field references is not applied recursively.

ambiguity.issue: 'Not applied recursively' is not defined; the following sentence suggests it means nested expressions (index values, encoding format parameters) are not covered, but it may also mean that presence checking operators nested in the operand do not inherit the rule. Chosen reading: the rule covers only the outermost ExtendedFieldReference of the operand.
readings: Error suppression applies only to the resolution of the ExtendedFieldReference of the operand itself, not to errors inside expressions nested in it.
Error suppression is not propagated to presence checking operators or references nested inside the operand.

requirements.subject: ent:error
requirements.canonical: An error occurring while resolving the value of an index inside index notation or the value of an encoding format parameter of a decoded field reference IS NOT suppressed by the presence checking error-handling rule.
requirements.original: Errors occurring during resolving a value of an index inside index notation or a value of an encoding format parameter of a decoded field reference are not affected by this rule.

requirements.subject: ent:ispresent-operator
requirements.canonical: The `ispresent` operator checks whether a referenced field is present in a data object.
requirements.original: The ispresent operator checks whether a referenced field is present in a data object.

requirements.subject: ent:ispresent-operator
requirements.canonical: The `ispresent` operator has the syntax `ispresent "(" TemplateInstance ")"`.
requirements.original: ispresent "(" TemplateInstance ")"

requirements.subject: ent:ispresent-operator

requirements.condition: the operand is a subfield of a template field set to AnyValue
requirements.canonical: When the operand of `ispresent` is a subfield of a template field to which AnyValue (`?`) is assigned, the template expansion mechanism of clause 15.6.2 IS applied before evaluating `ispresent`.
requirements.original: NOTE 1: When the argument of ispresent is a subfield of a template field to which the "?" (AnyValue) matching is assigned, the extension mechanism specified in clause 15.6.2 applies.
